title: If You Own AMD Stock ... GET READY!!
creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
summary: Jose Najarro defends AMD after a ~37.5% fall from its 52-week high, calling the 19 November Hunterbrook short report 'completely baloney' and laying out why he stays very bullish. The stock is still up ~90% year to date and ~97% over 52 weeks, so long-term holders are not sweating, he says. His bull case rests on three legs: a CPU shortage that should last a long time as AI agents drive tool-calling demand; AI accelerators, with the MI455 and Helios rack already shipping and ramping through 2027; and valuation, with a forward P/E of ~26 (about 23.5x calendar-2027 earnings) that he calls not crazy for the growth. He would buy more if AMD falls to ~$350-375. He then rebuts the short report point by point: the blacklisted-server firmware claim is unproven (the firmware is a public download, and CPUs face different export controls than GPUs); China/Hong Kong at 22% of FY25 sales and Singapore at 12.4% reflect billing location, not end demand, and Nvidia reported a similar 18% Singapore share in FY25 before restating; and the 320 million warrants to OpenAI and Meta vest only on compute milestones and are accretive to EPS from first revenue per management. He also defends the $48.8B of purchase commitments (up ~4x in three quarters) as locking in scarce wafers and capacity, and cites guidance of ~80% revenue growth in 2027. Nvidia appears only as a valuation comparison and Intel as a lagging competitor; no calls on either. (Some figures are garbled in the auto-captions.)

calls.thesis: Still very bullish on AMD despite the ~37.5% drop from its 52-week high; calls the Hunterbrook short report 'baloney' and would buy and increase his dollar-cost average if the stock falls to ~$350-375. CPU shortage plus the MI455/Helios AI accelerator ramp and a forward P/E of ~26 make it attractive at that level.
calls.base_case: CPU shortage persists as AI agents drive tool-calling CPU demand; Helios racks are shipping with a big Q4 step-up; management guides ~80% revenue growth and a doubling of server revenue in 2027.
calls.bull_case: MI455 wins incremental AI accelerator share; OpenAI/Meta warrants are accretive to non-GAAP EPS from first revenue per management; the OpenAI compute buildout could be worth $120B+ of revenue; forward P/E falls to ~23.5x on calendar-2027 earnings.
calls.bear_case: Hunterbrook short report: AMD firmware found in blacklisted Chinese servers, China/Hong Kong 22% of FY25 sales, 320M warrants to OpenAI/Meta (~19.5% dilution), and ~$28B of guarantees/leases against ~$15.8B cash; AI-fatigue sell-off continues.
